## Read Event Boundary Dataset

---

```{r read data, echo=FALSE}
setwd('~/Desktop/ProjectsTracks/FRP_EventSegment/Analysis') # set your current directory
event_boundary_raw <- read_excel("event_boundary/EventBoundary_Summary.xlsx")
```

## Separate Data Based on Section (P vs. H)

---
```{r data preparation, echo=FALSE}
h_event <- event_boundary_raw[,c("Item_Gaps", "H_Score_Percentage")] %>% filter(!is.na(H_Score_Percentage)) 
p_event <- event_boundary_raw[,c("Item_Gaps", "P_Score_Percentage")] %>% filter(!is.na(P_Score_Percentage)) 
```

---

## 1D Gaussian Smoothing

---
```{r - H section}
# Extract event ratings
h_event_raw <- h_event$H_Score_Percentage

# Apply Gaussian Smoothing
h_smooth_agreement <- gaussianSmooth(h_event_raw, sigma = 0.5)

# Find local maxima (points higher than neighbors)
# This function returns the index of every peak
find_peaks <- function(x, min_height = -Inf, min_prom = 0) {
  n <- length(x)
  peaks <- integer(0)

  for (i in 2:(n-1)) {
    if (x[i] >= x[i-1] && x[i] >= x[i+1] && x[i] >= min_height) {
      peaks <- c(peaks, i)
    }
  }

  # optional: simple prominence filter
  if (min_prom > 0 && length(peaks) > 0) {
    keep <- sapply(peaks, function(i) {
      left_min  <- min(x[1:i])
      right_min <- min(x[i:n])
      (x[i] - max(left_min, right_min)) >= min_prom
    })
    peaks <- peaks[keep]
  }

  unique(peaks)
}

peaks_h <- find_peaks(h_smooth_agreement)
```


```{r H section visualization}
boundary_items_h <- c(2, 5, 8, 12, 17, 21)
x_labels_h <- ifelse(
  1:25 %in% boundary_items_h,
  paste0("<b><span style='color:#28BCC4'>", 1:25, "</span></b>"),
  1:25
)

# Visualization
ggplot(h_event, aes(x = Item_Gaps)) +
  # 1) Background Bars
  geom_col(
    aes(y = H_Score_Percentage, fill = "Raw agreement"),
    width = 0.85, alpha = 0.4
  ) +

  # 2) Smoothed curve
  # Added linetype mapping here to ensure it merges with the legend
  geom_line(
    aes(x = Item_Gaps, 
        y = h_smooth_agreement, color = "Gaussian-smoothed", linetype = "Gaussian-smoothed"),
    linewidth = 1.1, lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # 3) Boundary consensus (The actual lines)
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = peaks_h, 
    color = "#00BFC4", 
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.8, 
    alpha = 0.9
  ) +
  
  # 4) Legend Trick (The dummy segment)
  # Changed NA to 1 so ggplot doesn't complain about empty aesthetics
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 1, xend = 1, y = 1, yend = 1, 
        color = "Boundary consensus", linetype = "Boundary consensus"),
    alpha = 0 # Keeps it invisible
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Serial Item Transitions",
    y = "Proportion of Agreement",
    fill = NULL, color = NULL, linetype = NULL
  ) +

  # Manual scales
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Raw agreement at each transition" = "#9E9E9E")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Gaussian-smoothed"  = "#F8766D",
    "Boundary consensus" = "#00BFC4"
  )) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(
    "Boundary consensus" = "dashed",
    "Gaussian-smoothed"  = "solid"
  )) +
  
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        linetype = c("dashed", "solid"), # Matches Consensus, Gaussian order
        color = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"), # Force the colors
        alpha = 1,                       # Make legend keys opaque
        linewidth = 1
      )
    ),
    linetype = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        linetype = c("dashed", "solid"),
        color = c("#00BFC4", "#F8766D"),
        alpha = 1,
        linewidth = 1
      )
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:25, labels = x_labels_h) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1.05)) + 
  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "horizontal",
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0.5, "cm"), # Space between plot and legend
    axis.line = element_line(linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = 0.3)
  ) + 
  theme(
    axis.text.x = ggtext::element_markdown()
  )

# GGsave
ggsave(
  filename = "Event_Boundary_Agreement_H.pdf",
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  device = cairo_pdf   # Better font rendering than standard pdf
)
```


```{r - P section}
p_event_raw <- p_event$P_Score_Percentage
p_smooth_agreement <- gaussianSmooth(p_event_raw, sigma = 0.5)

# 2. Find local maxima (points higher than neighbors)
# This function returns the index of every peak
peaks_p <- find_peaks(p_smooth_agreement)
```

**The reason to use 1D Gaussian smoothing is because this boundary data is index (or item) based. KDE works on continuous data.

## Exploratory: Kernel Density Estimation for Event Segmentation

---
```{r KDE - H section, echo=FALSE}

# Draw Plot FIRST to capture coordinates
# -------------------------------------------------------
# We save the output of barplot() into a variable 'bp'. 
# 'bp' contains the exact X-coordinate of the center of every bar.
bp_h <- barplot(h_event$H_Score_Percentage, names.arg = h_event$Item_Gaps, las = 2, col = "lightblue", 
              main = "Boundary Agreement (Aligned) - H Section", ylim = c(0, 1))

# Calculate Density using 'bp' (Real Coordinates)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
h_event$norm_weights <- h_event$H_Score_Percentage/sum(h_event$H_Score_Percentage)


# Use 'bp' (the bar coordinates) instead of 1:length(scores)
kde_h <- density(bp_h, weights = h_event$norm_weights, bw = 0.7)

# Fix the Scaling Factor (Height)
# -------------------------------------------------------
# Because the bars are spread out (spacing > 1), the density curve gets flatter.
# We must multiply by the average spacing to regain the correct height.
spacing <- mean(diff(bp_h)) # Usually 1.2
scale_factor_h <- sum(h_event$H_Score_Percentage) * spacing

# 5. Draw the Line
# -------------------------------------------------------
lines(kde_h$x, kde_h$y * scale_factor_h, col = "red", lwd = 1.5)

```
```{r KDE - P section, echo=FALSE}

# Draw Plot FIRST to capture coordinates
# -------------------------------------------------------
# We save the output of barplot() into a variable 'bp'. 
# 'bp' contains the exact X-coordinate of the center of every bar.
bp_p <- barplot(p_event$P_Score_Percentage, names.arg = p_event$Item_Gaps, las = 2, col = "lightblue", 
              main = "Boundary Agreement (Aligned) - P Section", ylim = c(0, 1))

# Calculate Density using 'bp' (Real Coordinates)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
p_event$norm_weights <- p_event$P_Score_Percentage/sum(p_event$P_Score_Percentage)


# Use 'bp' (the bar coordinates) instead of 1:length(scores)
kde_p <- density(bp_p, weights = p_event$norm_weights, bw = 0.7)

# Fix the Scaling Factor (Height)
# -------------------------------------------------------
# Because the bars are spread out (spacing > 1), the density curve gets flatter.
# We must multiply by the average spacing to regain the correct height.
spacing <- mean(diff(bp_p)) 
scale_factor_p <- sum(p_event$P_Score_Percentage) * spacing

# 5. Draw the Line
# -------------------------------------------------------
lines(kde_p$x, kde_p$y * scale_factor_p, col = "red", lwd = 1.5)
```
